abstract.md: 'An abstract method is implicitly a virtual method.' virtual.md: 'When you invoke a virtual method, the runtime checks the type of the object for an overriding member. It calls the overriding member in the most derived class.' EmailNotifier declares no Send (source lines 21-25), so the inherited NotifierBase.Send runs and its Format call dispatches to EmailNotifier.Format.

private.md: 'You can access private members only within the body of the class or the struct where you declare them'. protected.md: 'You can access a protected member within its class and by derived class instances.'

abstract.md: 'A non-abstract class derived from an abstract class must include actual implementations of all inherited abstract methods and accessors.' Also: 'Non-abstract classes that derive from the abstract class must implement members marked as abstract.' (compiler error CS0534, refs misc/cs0534.md).

Conditional wording ('fits when one step varies ...; when steps vary independently, handing in objects scales better'), not an unconditioned ranking. Count follows from single inheritance (class.md: 'a class can inherit implementation from one base class only'): 2 wordings x 2 destinations = 4 subclasses; 3 x 2 = 6, so a third wording adds exactly two, as s5 now says. Consistent with quiz q6 (six now, eight with a fourth wording).

virtual.md: 'By default, methods are non-virtual. You can't override a non-virtual method.' cs0506.md: 'cannot override inherited member ... because it is not marked "virtual", "abstract", or "override"'. 'Marks as open to it' covers all three marks without naming virtual/override (depth_notes); NotifierBase.Send (stage-1 line 11, 'public void Send') carries none, and round-1 execution gave CS0506 for an override of it. Round 2 checked only changed parts: s2, s4 p3, s5 split, s7 step 4/expected, summary 3, quiz q1 c, q6 b (sealed.md:13 confirms q1 c); both round-1 majors resolved.

issues.text: Round 2, changed parts only. This sentence closes the round-1 gap and I can follow it: only a marked method can be overridden, Format is marked, Send is not. I only wonder briefly whether some mark other than `abstract` exists that the author could have put on Send; the CS0506 step in Try it answers this in practice, so it does not block me.
issues.quote: In C#, a subclass can override only a method the base class marks as open to it, as `abstract` does for `Format`; `Send` carries no such mark, so only `Format` is open.
issues.fix: Optional, no change required: end the sentence with a short clause saying that leaving `Send` unmarked is the base-class author's choice, so the order is decided in `NotifierBase`.
